Later you see Markus and Björn standing peacefully together over a coffee. As you go past, Markus whispers to Björn: 'Tell me... what was that earlier with Miller and the red ball?' - 'No idea. But my pulse was down to 60 straight afterwards. The man has an aura.'
sidequests/sq_boss_fight_hallway_2a/opts/0/r  ·  df3c3b234713.opus  ·  109 Zeichen
You give the pair of them a knowing nod, say nothing and walk on. The office grapevine has made you a legend.
sidequests/sq_boss_fight_hallway_2b/text  ·  f4f77922bdd7.opus  ·  236 Zeichen
Your attempt at mediation has had a bizarre effect: Markus and Björn have made common cause over their shared hatred of IT. Both of them now block your bug reports. 'IT is not a priority', Markus says to Björn in the corridor, laughing.
sidequests/sq_boss_fight_hallway_2b/opts/0/r  ·  54569f36b02d.opus  ·  142 Zeichen
You kill their VPN certificates. Let them carry on sniping offline. Your aggression drops briefly, and there will be nasty emails before long.
sidequests/sq_boss_fight_hallway_2b/opts/1/r  ·  a34f92dc6d38.opus  ·  82 Zeichen
You have no strength for turf wars. You let them talk and simply carry on working.
sidequests/sq_boss_fight_hallway_2c/text  ·  d2d381f9c2ee.opus  ·  175 Zeichen
Because you took the long way round through the old basement, you discover a dusty box in the boiler room. Inside is entirely unused old IT kit that somebody forgot years ago.
sidequests/sq_boss_fight_hallway_2c/opts/0/r  ·  a5d8100cad5e.opus  ·  49 Zeichen
Half a packet of black cable ties. Always useful.
sidequests/sq_boss_fight_hallway_2c/opts/1/r  ·  b54f78337368.opus  ·  75 Zeichen
A first-class crosshead. The universe rewards the path of least resistance.
sidequests/sq_printer_jam_1/text  ·  57ca711e3999.opus  ·  152 Zeichen
The big department printer is beeping hysterically: 'Paper jam in tray 3'. An angry cluster of staff stands in front of it. Nobody dares open the hatch.
sidequests/sq_printer_jam_1/opts/0/r  ·  1f3e563240a8.opus  ·  108 Zeichen
You pull at torn shreds of paper deep inside. Your hands are covered in toner, and the machine prints again.
sidequests/sq_printer_jam_1/opts/1/r  ·  996668a07c3a.opus  ·  118 Zeichen
You open the thick book and read aloud: 'Repairs by certified specialist personnel only!' The crowd falls back in awe.
sidequests/sq_printer_jam_1/opts/2/r  ·  46350ce093ea.opus  ·  114 Zeichen
You hang up an 'OUT OF ORDER' sign like a professional. Problem delegated. Nobody is printing anything else today.
sidequests/sq_printer_jam_2a/text  ·  c75ac7942ced.opus  ·  177 Zeichen
Your hands are completely black with toner. On the way to the washroom you run into the CEO. He wants to shake your hand cheerfully to congratulate you on your work anniversary.
sidequests/sq_printer_jam_2a/opts/0/r  ·  098910e97640.opus  ·  96 Zeichen
You shake his hand. He stares in horror at his ruined fingers. You have just buried a promotion.
sidequests/sq_printer_jam_2a/opts/1/r  ·  620806bcbc1a.opus  ·  96 Zeichen
You raise your hands defensively. He nods understandingly. 'Ah, IT at the front line. Carry on!'
sidequests/sq_printer_jam_2b/text  ·  07819d99ef03.opus  ·  206 Zeichen
Because of your 'specialist personnel' remark, an eager colleague has actually called out external support. The engineer stands there, pulls a sheet of paper out of the printer and presents a bill for €250.
sidequests/sq_printer_jam_2b/opts/0/r  ·  e64875d0d6b1.opus  ·  135 Zeichen
You bond with the external IT man. The two of you laugh about the incompetence of the workforce. Good for the soul, bad for the budget.
sidequests/sq_printer_jam_2b/opts/1/r  ·  5e5a7e63e6db.opus  ·  97 Zeichen
You explain to Accounts that the users reacted in a panic. Ms Elster rages. You are in the clear.
sidequests/sq_printer_jam_2c/text  ·  b39b9a3eb4f3.opus  ·  176 Zeichen
Since the department printer is 'broken', five colleagues are now standing in your office wanting you to print their extremely important documents on your little local printer.
sidequests/sq_printer_jam_2c/opts/0/r  ·  159398493d3d.opus  ·  82 Zeichen
For half an hour you print contracts for other people. Your toner cartridge weeps.
sidequests/sq_printer_jam_2c/opts/1/r  ·  a72ace0293e8.opus  ·  83 Zeichen
You simply pull the USB cable out and shrug. The colleagues withdraw, disappointed.
sidequests/sq_crying_intern_1/text  ·  9211efcab961.opus  ·  151 Zeichen

sidequests/sq_crying_intern_1/opts/0/r  ·  a352613ae8e9.opus  ·  89 Zeichen
You press the chocolate into his hand. The chewing calms him at once and he stops crying.
sidequests/sq_crying_intern_1/opts/1/r  ·  0658545e4b18.opus  ·  175 Zeichen
You sit down at his desk, dig deep into the file system and rescue the file. Film music plays in your head while you do it. Hollywood could hardly have staged it more tensely.
sidequests/sq_crying_intern_1/opts/2/r  ·  11641d1602ad.opus  ·  104 Zeichen
Learning through pain. You pat his shoulder and say: 'You may as well start packing up your coffee mug.'
sidequests/sq_crying_intern_2a/text  ·  480d63e1fe1b.opus  ·  117 Zeichen
The intern is in front of you again. 'The chocolate was great, thanks! But the file is still gone. What do I do now?'
sidequests/sq_crying_intern_2a/opts/0/r  ·  a994ed872ae7.opus  ·  81 Zeichen
You restore the file from a backup. Your kindness costs you a great deal of time.
sidequests/sq_crying_intern_2a/opts/1/r  ·  9c0ee2f9f5de.opus  ·  88 Zeichen
Stupidity punishes itself. He sits down at PowerPoint, sobbing, and starts from scratch.
sidequests/sq_crying_intern_2b/text  ·  3f6ba30e2239.opus  ·  157 Zeichen
You did rescue the presentation, and on opening it you establish that it was not a CEO presentation at all. It is a collection of cat memes for 'Fun Friday'.
sidequests/sq_crying_intern_2b/opts/0/r  ·  cc316be494e0.opus  ·  95 Zeichen
You bawl him out for wasting half an hour of your time on jokes. He will avoid you from now on.
sidequests/sq_crying_intern_2b/opts/1/r  ·  45f1f2acc9a4.opus  ·  89 Zeichen
You quickly knock up a picture of a crying intern and slip it in. Humour in IT runs dark.
sidequests/sq_crying_intern_2c/text  ·  6eab3a9cd2b6.opus  ·  170 Zeichen
In his panic at you, the intern really did pack his things and leave. HR rings: 'Miller! What did you say to the poor boy?! We have to advertise the post all over again!'
sidequests/sq_crying_intern_2c/opts/0/r  ·  1c480d5996e7.opus  ·  105 Zeichen
You put it down to general performance pressure. The company wonders whether the onboarding is too harsh.
sidequests/sq_crying_intern_2c/opts/1/r  ·  e47313d1e61c.opus  ·  95 Zeichen
You paint him as an incompetent risk. HR grumbles, and cannot touch you on the technical facts.
sidequests/sq_wrong_delivery_1/text  ·  ebd76be87f64.opus  ·  173 Zeichen
A Lieferando courier hurriedly presses a brown paper bag into your hand in passing. 'One pastrami sandwich for... er, the third floor! Have a good day!' He vanishes outside.
sidequests/sq_wrong_delivery_1/opts/0/r  ·  8f55c0929b35.opus  ·  140 Zeichen
Good-naturedly you walk through every office, and nobody will admit to ordering a sandwich. From admin to postman, and not a word of thanks.
sidequests/sq_wrong_delivery_1/opts/1/r  ·  a34fb22c4fea.opus  ·  70 Zeichen
Not your sandwich, not your problem. You put it on the counter and go.
sidequests/sq_wrong_delivery_1/opts/2/r  ·  af05eed21eaa.opus  ·  158 Zeichen
You take the bag to your office and slide it into the bottom drawer. Free lunch at the company's expense! It already smells all the way out into the corridor.
sidequests/sq_wrong_delivery_2a/text  ·  aa4cfb25deb3.opus  ·  142 Zeichen
Ms Elster rings. 'Mr Miller, did you happen to see the courier downstairs? My pastrami sandwich, ordered at company expense, has disappeared!'
sidequests/sq_wrong_delivery_2a/opts/0/r  ·  a512c92106da.opus  ·  88 Zeichen
You sacrifice your loot. She is delighted. Your hunger is massive and so is your temper.
sidequests/sq_wrong_delivery_2a/opts/1/r  ·  0ece6d3f25e3.opus  ·  96 Zeichen
You brush a crumb off your mouth. She will hate the delivery service, and you are full and safe.
sidequests/sq_wrong_delivery_2b/text  ·  95f7ad8ab32d.opus  ·  165 Zeichen
After 15 minutes of pointless searching across the whole third floor, you still have the sandwich. It is slowly going cold and the grease is soaking through the bag.
sidequests/sq_wrong_delivery_2b/opts/0/r  ·  6c8db4f0524c.opus  ·  58 Zeichen
It tastes fantastic, even lukewarm. Your aggression drops.
sidequests/sq_wrong_delivery_2b/opts/1/r  ·  e235184f3104.opus  ·  74 Zeichen
On principle you do not eat other people's food. You throw €15 in the bin.
sidequests/sq_wrong_delivery_2c/text  ·  eca9bf45b10e.opus  ·  115 Zeichen
The bag stood on the counter in the sun for hours. The whole entrance area now smells unpleasantly of old pastrami.
sidequests/sq_wrong_delivery_2c/opts/0/r  ·  9096546f28f6.opus  ·  102 Zeichen
Egon curses for minutes about the 'filthy animals' in this company. You agree with him hypocritically.
sidequests/sq_wrong_delivery_2c/opts/1/r  ·  0d4ea2239831.opus  ·  65 Zeichen
You avoid the lobby entirely. What you do not see does not exist.
sidequests/sq_drafty_door_1/text  ·  f70ef79ec137.opus  ·  170 Zeichen
The automatic sliding door to the courtyard is broken and stands permanently open. An icy wind blows down the corridor. Colleagues sit at their desks in scarves and hats.
sidequests/sq_drafty_door_1/opts/0/r  ·  0ff3fedc29fc.opus  ·  88 Zeichen
Egon turns up after 15 minutes, curses the technology and kicks the door. It stays open.
sidequests/sq_drafty_door_1/opts/1/r  ·  335ffca87a48.opus  ·  113 Zeichen
You lash the glass panels tightly together. The draught has gone, and nobody can get into the courtyard any more.
sidequests/sq_drafty_door_1/opts/2/r  ·  1990a4d9a044.opus  ·  89 Zeichen
One strip of tape across the motion sensor. The door closes immediately. Gloriously warm.
sidequests/sq_drafty_door_2a/text  ·  01cfb5bc735c.opus  ·  163 Zeichen
A manager wanted to get out to the courtyard for a smoke. He forced his way against your fixed cable ties and now the sliding door's guide rail is completely bent.
sidequests/sq_drafty_door_2a/opts/0/r  ·  c9291b4c7ee1.opus  ·  114 Zeichen
You take photographs and report him. He is furious, and the boss praises your eye for protecting company property.
sidequests/sq_drafty_door_2a/opts/1/r  ·  735c88f16456.opus  ·  61 Zeichen
You dispose of the evidence. The door is now broken AND open.
sidequests/sq_drafty_door_2b/text  ·  c269e1a9f8b9.opus  ·  187 Zeichen
Your tape trick was too good. The door will not open at all from outside. Three smokers stand freezing in the courtyard, hammering on the glass in a panic because they cannot get back in.
sidequests/sq_drafty_door_2b/opts/0/r  ·  55bf0abec5a9.opus  ·  61 Zeichen
A magnificent moment. Smoking damages your health, after all.
sidequests/sq_drafty_door_2b/opts/1/r  ·  29da740b7dde.opus  ·  61 Zeichen
You peel the tape off. They tumble in, frozen, and thank you.
sidequests/sq_drafty_door_2c/text  ·  2769c37eca18.opus  ·  171 Zeichen
Egon has given up on the door. Instead he has put a gigantic, loud, red building-site fan heater in the corridor. It draws so much current that the ceiling lights flicker.
sidequests/sq_drafty_door_2c/opts/0/r  ·  6f1d1007fba1.opus  ·  70 Zeichen
The server circuit matters more to you than warm feet in the corridor.
sidequests/sq_drafty_door_2c/opts/1/r  ·  efd71cb22bcd.opus  ·  50 Zeichen
You spend 10 minutes at the warm source. Glorious.
sidequests/sq_elearning_1/text  ·  644ef6c6e57d.opus  ·  252 Zeichen
Sabine from HR sends a system lock. 'The annual compliance training 'Synergetic Sitting' is overdue!' An unskippable video module starts on your main monitor. It lasts exactly 90 minutes and checks with a click every 5 minutes that you are still awake.
sidequests/sq_elearning_1/opts/0/r  ·  10dd8e599ac1.opus  ·  167 Zeichen
You stare for 90 minutes at a man in a polo neck talking about lumbar vertebrae. Every 5 minutes you click 'I am still here'. Your aggression simmers, and HR is happy.
sidequests/sq_elearning_1/opts/1/r  ·  3facc7aea465.opus  ·  140 Zeichen
You log into the back end and set the value against your name to 'Passed'. Takes 5 minutes. If that comes out in an audit, you are finished.
sidequests/sq_elearning_1/opts/2/r  ·  50ad6db667c0.opus  ·  107 Zeichen
You clip your watch to the mouse, put your feet on the desk and doze off. The 90 minutes pass like a dream.
sidequests/sq_elearning_2a/text  ·  37f2b81faba5.opus  ·  146 Zeichen
The boss comes into your office. 'Miller, HR reports that you scored 100% on the video's reflex tests. You must be a master of ergonomic sitting!'
sidequests/sq_elearning_2a/opts/0/r  ·  7da1ab39583a.opus  ·  67 Zeichen
He waves it away. 'Health comes first, Miller.' You roll your eyes.
sidequests/sq_elearning_2a/opts/1/r  ·  29a7658766e5.opus  ·  111 Zeichen
You draw yourself up. The boss nods his approval. The pain of those 90 minutes was at least good for the image.
sidequests/sq_elearning_2b/text  ·  43ea83e9cd86.opus  ·  146 Zeichen
Sabine (HR) rings. 'Mr Miller? Our system shows that you completed the 90-minute video in exactly 14 seconds. Have you been hacking the software?'
sidequests/sq_elearning_2b/opts/0/r  ·  897ae20cc995.opus  ·  141 Zeichen
You waffle about 'asynchronous timestamps in the server'. Sabine understands nothing and gives up. 'IT and their errors...', she sighs. Phew.
sidequests/sq_elearning_2b/opts/1/r  ·  9aebfb66f6f9.opus  ·  138 Zeichen
You criticise the HR software sharply. She is offended and forwards your message — verbatim, to the boss, with the note 'for information'.
sidequests/sq_elearning_2c/text  ·  25b47b8b2e9d.opus  ·  197 Zeichen
You thought you had gone unnoticed. Markus from Sales is leaning in the doorway, grinning. 'Have a nice sleep, Sleeping Beauty? I heard you snoring as I went past. What is my silence worth to you?'
sidequests/sq_elearning_2c/opts/0/r  ·  f5bb43c3a2c6.opus  ·  138 Zeichen
You threaten him back. Markus raises his hands. 'Whoa, steady on, tiger. It was only a joke.' He leaves, and the relationship is poisoned.
sidequests/sq_elearning_2c/opts/1/r  ·  92e7d7249017.opus  ·  74 Zeichen
Markus takes the doughnut. 'Bribery? Accepted.' He bites into it and goes.
sidequests/sq_workout_1/text  ·  ff39db2cd298.opus  ·  276 Zeichen
You are on an errand on the third floor. When you look into the marketing office, your blood runs cold. Half the department is lying on the floor, twitching wildly, eyes rolled back, groaning loudly. It looks like a major medical emergency or a collective summoning of demons!
sidequests/sq_workout_1/opts/0/r  ·  001617cbb563.opus  ·  153 Zeichen
You bellow 'PARAMEDICS!' and dial 112. Chantal sits up, irritated. 'Are you mad?! This is 'Agile Floor Pilates'! You are ruining our flow!' Embarrassing.
sidequests/sq_workout_1/opts/1/r  ·  6bf36f54af06.opus  ·  184 Zeichen
You simply lie down with them. For 90 minutes you twitch and stretch unproductively on the carpet. It is bizarre, the time flies past, and your back cracks in a way that sets you free.
sidequests/sq_workout_1/opts/2/r  ·  e9c8645d9e67.opus  ·  134 Zeichen
You lean against the doorframe, bite into your chocolate and watch the absurd spectacle at leisure for 30 minutes, like a documentary.
sidequests/sq_dance_2a/text  ·  19da3f58530b.opus  ·  244 Zeichen
You walk down the corridor hunched and ashamed. A colleague from Sales points at you and laughs so hard he cannot breathe. 'There he is! The fleeing dancer! The GIF of your panicked face after the moonwalk already has 10,000 views on LinkedIn!'
sidequests/sq_dance_2a/opts/0/r  ·  e6683f5f5771.opus  ·  137 Zeichen
You put a brave face on it and laugh along. That takes the sting out of the joke. People respect you for being able to laugh at yourself.
sidequests/sq_dance_2a/opts/1/r  ·  ca075dbd8111.opus  ·  84 Zeichen
You give him the finger and go. Now people laugh behind your back. You are seething.
sidequests/sq_dance_2b/text  ·  3e3fa87bc465.opus  ·  210 Zeichen
Chantal from Marketing all but leaps into your arms in the corridor. 'Miller! Your dance! The investors love our young, dynamic culture. The clip is going completely viral! The boss says you are to do PR work!'
sidequests/sq_dance_2b/opts/0/r  ·  a0dcd2d59f7f.opus  ·  92 Zeichen
You push Chantal away and flee back to real work. You have thrown away an epic career boost.
sidequests/sq_dance_2b/opts/1/r  ·  7b02b20381f2.opus  ·  145 Zeichen
You become the mascot. You spend a solid hour waving at cameras and taking selfies. An enormous waste of time, and your ego and the boss love it.
sidequests/sq_awkward_2a/text  ·  a09703762b08.opus  ·  238 Zeichen

sidequests/sq_awkward_2a/opts/0/r  ·  bf22488d0f23.opus  ·  143 Zeichen
You try to explain. Chantal nods slowly. 'Of course... 'stuck'. Very creative, Miller.' Nobody believes you. Your reputation has taken a knock.
sidequests/sq_awkward_2a/opts/1/r  ·  837ce8b08598.opus  ·  121 Zeichen
You turn round and run. Which of course looks like an admission of guilt. The rumour mill really goes into overdrive now.
sidequests/sq_awkward_2b/text  ·  0a7de023d92d.opus  ·  190 Zeichen

sidequests/sq_awkward_2b/opts/0/r  ·  d27999583b0d.opus  ·  131 Zeichen

sidequests/sq_awkward_2b/opts/1/r  ·  8352e2c03c8f.opus  ·  98 Zeichen
You press 'delete'. Kevin nods coolly. 'Good call, boomer.' The apprentice has just dominated you.
sidequests/sq_fire_ext_1/text  ·  125644ad57d2.opus  ·  319 Zeichen
On your rounds you enter office 312. The room is empty, but there is an acrid smell of melted plastic and burnt cheese. A fire extinguisher stands abandoned in the middle of the room. On the desk a completely destroyed, illegal sandwich toaster is smouldering away. The culprit evidently put it out in a panic and fled.
sidequests/sq_fire_ext_1/opts/0/r  ·  1eed220d1070.opus  ·  153 Zeichen
Better safe than sorry! You pull the lever and engulf the toaster (and half the desk) in a thick white snowscape of CO2 powder. That felt extremely good!
sidequests/sq_fire_ext_1/opts/1/r  ·  67c1718e8e55.opus  ·  157 Zeichen

sidequests/sq_fire_ext_1/opts/2/r  ·  d8e491a9ea75.opus  ·  170 Zeichen

sidequests/sq_fire_ext_2a/text  ·  841e850978c7.opus  ·  269 Zeichen
Kevin comes rushing at you in a panic. 'Boss! Have you seen the fire extinguisher from office 312 by any chance?! I made myself a cheese toastie in there in secret and it caught fire. I was about to hang it back so Egon the caretaker would not notice, and it has gone!'
sidequests/sq_fire_ext_2a/opts/0/r  ·  4d7cd6a0c60f.opus  ·  214 Zeichen
Kevin's eyes go wide. 'GPS?! Oh God, HR will know exactly that it was last with me!' He forgets the search instantly and sprints off to work out a watertight alibi for the time of the offence. You grin to yourself.
sidequests/sq_fire_ext_2a/opts/1/r  ·  92a31ab2da3f.opus  ·  157 Zeichen
Kevin goes chalk white. 'Oh my God. I am dead. Egon will wall me up in the boiler room!' He runs off in tears. You have your peace and your new tool is safe.

sidequests/sq_fire_ext_2b/opts/0/r  ·  ed629d501899.opus  ·  160 Zeichen

sidequests/sq_fire_ext_2b/opts/1/r  ·  ced536882786.opus  ·  157 Zeichen

sidequests/sq_fire_ext_2c/text  ·  531c535804c6.opus  ·  251 Zeichen

sidequests/sq_fire_ext_2c/opts/0/r  ·  e7f458ac84a0.opus  ·  149 Zeichen

sidequests/sq_fire_ext_2c/opts/1/r  ·  e5a9c4c28505.opus  ·  150 Zeichen

sidequests/sq_plant_2a/opts/0/r  ·  8d7a8887e4a2.opus  ·  97 Zeichen

sidequests/sq_plant_2a/opts/1/r  ·  44a2b35b96d2.opus  ·  116 Zeichen

sidequests/sq_moving_box/opts/0/r  ·  05dabdce75e5.opus  ·  171 Zeichen
You carry it to the skip. Halfway there Ms Elster comes past and gives you an approving nod. Two hours later there is a new box in the corridor. On it: 'DO NOT THROW OUT'.
sidequests/sq_moving_box/opts/1/r  ·  6faaf9ced7e5.opus  ·  173 Zeichen
Two coffee mugs with dried-up contents, a ring binder marked 'Q3 2018' and, right at the bottom, a screwdriver. You take the screwdriver. The mugs you leave, out of respect.
sidequests/sq_moving_box/opts/2/r  ·  1e0fd228ecc7.opus  ·  164 Zeichen
Right at the bottom, under a layer of promotional pens, lies a Windows 95 manual. Rüdiger has written on the first page: 'In case anybody ever asks again.' He knew.
sidequests/sq_empty_desk/text  ·  79f22661c157.opus  ·  178 Zeichen
A desk in the open-plan office stands empty. Monitor dark, chair pushed in neatly. The top drawer is open a crack. Inside: duct tape, a USB stick and a packet of glucose tablets.
sidequests/sq_empty_desk/opts/0/r  ·  2951873ac6d3.opus  ·  203 Zeichen
Pocketed. At that moment somebody comes round the corner with a coffee mug, sits down at that very desk and boots the machine up. He was at lunch. The two of you look at each other. Nobody says anything.
sidequests/sq_empty_desk/opts/1/r  ·  677cc540837c.opus  ·  142 Zeichen
An unlabelled stick. Could be a boot stick, could equally be somebody's private photo collection. You pocket it and resolve never to find out.
sidequests/sq_empty_desk/opts/2/r  ·  e45f5817e39e.opus  ·  157 Zeichen
You push it shut. Later in the day you hear somebody swearing because his tape has vanished. Not yours. For the first time today, moral superiority is yours.
sidequests/sq_raum_phoenix/text  ·  26b87d601385.opus  ·  261 Zeichen
Room 'Creative 2' has been continuously booked in the system for four months: 'Project Phoenix, all day, recurring booking'. You pass it on your rounds. The room is empty. It is always empty. And nobody in the whole building has ever heard of a Project Phoenix.
sidequests/sq_raum_phoenix/opts/0/r  ·  811818dad6e6.opus  ·  192 Zeichen
Four months of blockade, ended with three clicks. The room is free and triple-booked within the hour. And somewhere in this building somebody has just noticed that their cover has disappeared.
sidequests/sq_raum_phoenix/opts/1/r  ·  7c36d61b5b3f.opus  ·  238 Zeichen
A permanently booked, permanently empty room is the quietest place in the company. You do an hour of paperwork there undisturbed, in heavenly silence. Whoever Phoenix is: the two of you now share a hiding place without knowing each other.
sidequests/sq_raum_phoenix/opts/2/r  ·  2ab4fa2409b9.opus  ·  210 Zeichen
Gabi looks left, looks right, and drops her voice: 'Do not ask about Phoenix. But IF you ask: it has to do with the third floor. And with Mr Rademacher.' There is no Mr Rademacher in this company. Not any more.
sidequests/sq_raum_phoenix_2a/text  ·  78ca7d8bc2ed.opus  ·  261 Zeichen
The next morning there is a Post-it on your monitor. Clean block capitals: 'The booking was DELIBERATE. You do not know what you have done. - P.' No sender, no witnesses, and the camera in the corridor points in exactly the wrong direction. It would, naturally.
sidequests/sq_raum_phoenix_2a/opts/0/r  ·  559b6a4eb36c.opus  ·  279 Zeichen
You refuse to be intimidated by stationery. The room stays free. Over the following days small things start to register: your office chair is set differently in the mornings. Your window blind jams. Your name in the booking system suddenly has a typo in it. War takes many forms.
sidequests/sq_raum_phoenix_2a/opts/1/r  ·  fb73a798d839.opus  ·  227 Zeichen
You spend your lunch break hidden behind the flipchart in Creative 2. Nobody comes. Naturally nobody comes. As you give up in exasperation and leave, there is a second Post-it on the table: 'Nice try.' It was not there earlier.
sidequests/sq_raum_phoenix_2a/opts/2/r  ·  916fb4b2db02.opus  ·  257 Zeichen
You obey a Post-it. The recurring booking is running again, the room is officially occupied and genuinely empty, and the order of things is restored. In the afternoon a shrink-wrapped slice of streusel cake is lying on your keyboard. Phoenix says thank you.
sidequests/sq_raum_phoenix_2b/text  ·  c747fa7b9a26.opus  ·  243 Zeichen
You are sitting in the silent Phoenix room again when the door opens: Egon. With a flask, a newspaper and the composure of a man who has a standing appointment. The two of you stare at each other. 'You', says Egon slowly, 'are not Rademacher.'
sidequests/sq_raum_phoenix_2b/opts/0/r  ·  6c92edeb84c9.opus  ·  275 Zeichen
'Four months of recurring booking for a nap, Egon?' He folds the newspaper, stands up and leaves without a word. From next week the room really is free. The heating in your office, meanwhile, has taken to 'jamming' remarkably often, and Egon unfortunately never has a moment.
sidequests/sq_raum_phoenix_2b/opts/1/r  ·  ee6a6fa61551.opus  ·  237 Zeichen
The man has ruled this building for decades - he has simply earned himself a quiet room. You pack your things up. At the door Egon says, without looking up: 'Wednesdays I am not here.' It is an invitation. The largest one he has to give.
sidequests/sq_raum_phoenix_2b/opts/2/r  ·  52e8c099a735.opus  ·  237 Zeichen
The two of you settle it without many words: Egon keeps his lunchtime peace, you get the room on Tuesdays and Thursdays. How he books it through the account of a man who left in 2016 you do not ask. Some contracts only work unquestioned.
sidequests/sq_raum_phoenix_2c/text  ·  0d1705e1887e.opus  ·  225 Zeichen
You dig: Rademacher, head of IT until 2016, your predecessor's predecessor. His user account has never been disabled. It books rooms. It holds valid access rights. And according to the logs it answered an email nine days ago.
sidequests/sq_raum_phoenix_2c/opts/0/r  ·  9a024d80e6c2.opus  ·  287 Zeichen
Gabi listens and goes a shade paler. 'So it is true after all.' She says nothing more. On the way back it occurs to you that Gabi knows everything as a matter of principle and tells everything as a matter of principle - except on this one subject. That information is itself information.
sidequests/sq_raum_phoenix_2c/opts/1/r  ·  96a01e8312a6.opus  ·  237 Zeichen
While disabling it you find: 4,213 unread emails, a forwarding rule to an external address and a calendar full of recurring meetings with no end date. You end it all, document it cleanly and feel as though you have pensioned off a ghost.
sidequests/sq_raum_phoenix_2c/opts/2/r  ·  ba2299d043a9.opus  ·  216 Zeichen
'Dear Mr Rademacher, who is using this account?' No reply. Not all day. Then at 17:58 an automatic out-of-office notice: 'In a meeting. Room Creative 2.' You resolve to put no further questions to the building today.
sidequests/sq_gemba_walk/text  ·  b9619df6e5c4.opus  ·  286 Zeichen
Dr Wichtig has read a book. 'I am doing a GEMBA WALK today, Miller. Japanese management method. I observe the value streams. Simply act as though I were not here.' He stations himself a metre behind you. With a clipboard. You can hear him breathing and, at irregular intervals, writing.
sidequests/sq_gemba_walk/opts/0/r  ·  9ec1e515f2e8.opus  ·  241 Zeichen
You open three terminals, let impressive logs rush past and mutter things like 'latency anomaly in the east cluster'. There is no east cluster. Dr Wichtig takes enthusiastic notes. You have done no work at all, and it looked like the future.
sidequests/sq_gemba_walk/opts/1/r  ·  fb710fa3ec81.opus  ·  211 Zeichen
Under your guidance Dr Wichtig plugs in a network cable. It clicks. He beams like a child at the waterworks. 'I have TOUCHED the infrastructure, Miller.' That sentence will have consequences. Good ones? Unclear.
sidequests/sq_gemba_walk/opts/2/r  ·  e1587131deeb.opus  ·  244 Zeichen
The ball absorbs whatever the breathing behind you produces. You carry on working in perfect calm, as though the metre behind you were uninhabited. Dr Wichtig notes: 'Employee appears conspicuously calm.' That will end up in the report as well.
sidequests/sq_gemba_walk/opts/3/r  ·  3b80d7474bc1.opus  ·  210 Zeichen
You work under observation. Every keystroke feels like an examination, every error message like a confession. After a quarter of an hour he writes something conspicuously long. You will never want to know what.
sidequests/sq_gemba_walk_2a/text  ·  883b9937d142.opus  ·  268 Zeichen
The all-staff email 'Findings from the Gemba Walk' has arrived. Key finding on IT: 'The employee spends an estimated 40% of his time WAITING for progress bars. Proposal: procure faster bars.' The proposal is meant seriously. The distribution list is the whole company.
sidequests/sq_gemba_walk_2a/opts/0/r  ·  9f112ff13e03.opus  ·  241 Zeichen
'Excellent observation. Faster bars require faster storage.' Two days later a budget for SSDs is approved that you have been applying for these two years. There are times when you simply have to accept the language of management as a cipher.
sidequests/sq_gemba_walk_2a/opts/1/r  ·  209061a173df.opus  ·  249 Zeichen
The report goes into the folder with the other reports. Already in there are the 'Digitalisation Roadmap 2023' and the concept paper 'The Paperless Office' (18 pages, printed out). Silence is an answer too. The trouble is that the boss remembers it.
sidequests/sq_gemba_walk_2a/opts/2/r  ·  5c6588d60ecf.opus  ·  230 Zeichen
In a matter-of-fact reply you explain the difference between the display and the cause. It is the politest email of your life on the nature of time. Dr Wichtig replies: 'Understood. Faster causes, then.' You give up. With dignity.
sidequests/sq_gemba_walk_2b/text  ·  ba4402002ff3.opus  ·  284 Zeichen
Your fake activity has been presented to the board as a 'model example of focused work' - complete with a photograph of you in front of three terminals. Other departments are now to adopt 'the Miller Terminal Principle'. There are already queries about what the Terminal Principle is.
sidequests/sq_gemba_walk_2b/opts/0/r  ·  bc5a3ec9432b.opus  ·  245 Zeichen
You train twelve administrative staff in looking impressively busy. Disguised as 'focus techniques' it is the most honest course in company history, because that is precisely what everybody here practises anyway. The feedback forms: outstanding.
sidequests/sq_gemba_walk_2b/opts/1/r  ·  bcd73735356d.opus  ·  224 Zeichen
'That was... theatre?' Dr Wichtig looks stricken at his clipboard, where the model example is written down. 'I showed it to the BOARD, Miller.' Honesty has its price, and the exchange rate against the board is poor just now.
sidequests/sq_gemba_walk_2b/opts/2/r  ·  2a7c7491f7ca.opus  ·  276 Zeichen
Chantal turns the misunderstanding into a product: 'Deep Work Sessions powered by IT', with a sign-up list and a playlist. People now sit voluntarily in silence in front of screens and call it professional development. Everybody is happy. Nobody is working. Business as usual.
sidequests/sq_gemba_walk_2c/text  ·  d843c74a579f.opus  ·  262 Zeichen
Dr Wichtig now tells the story of the network cable in every gathering ('It CLICKED, gentlemen'). Now he is in the doorway again: he would like a 'monthly hands-on hour in the infrastructure'. He has already bought his own little screwdriver. He shows it to you.
sidequests/sq_gemba_walk_2c/opts/0/r  ·  facc099e3cee.opus  ·  254 Zeichen
Kevin and Dr Wichtig, together at the patch panel: an alliance of boundless enthusiasm and no idea whatsoever, in both directions. They get on splendidly. Kevin now calls him 'Doc'. You have either created something wonderful or a monster. Probably both.
sidequests/sq_gemba_walk_2c/opts/1/r  ·  3817ba6a1906.opus  ·  271 Zeichen
Once a month the CEO plugs in harmless cables under supervision and is afterwards more approachable than ever. Side effect: anyone who watches the boss patching suddenly gets every IT budget waved through. The most expensive hour of the month is also the most profitable.
sidequests/sq_gemba_walk_2c/opts/2/r  ·  e29fc4ff63f1.opus  ·  243 Zeichen
'Access for certified personnel only, Doctor. Insurance requirement.' He withdraws, disappointed, the little screwdriver still in his hand. You have done the right thing and you still feel as though you had cancelled a child's trip to the zoo.
sidequests/sq_gemba_walk_2d/text  ·  258470828ba2.opus  ·  239 Zeichen
The Gemba report has consequences: your recorded calmness has caught HR's attention. 'We are planning a resilience workshop', the email purrs, 'and would love to have you as an internal keynote contributor. What is your secret, Mr Miller?'
sidequests/sq_gemba_walk_2d/opts/0/r  ·  d9130bff1cbf.opus  ·  222 Zeichen
'My secret is that I come here to work.' HR finds the answer 'refreshingly authentic' and pencils you in for a future format called 'Radical Honesty'. There is no escaping a workshop here. You only get to choose its title.
sidequests/sq_gemba_walk_2d/opts/1/r  ·  8733f302db36.opus  ·  259 Zeichen
You present the stress ball. HR is delighted with the 'low-threshold solution' and orders two hundred of them with the company logo on. As keynote contributor you are handed the first one. It squeaks slightly. The old one was better. Now you have two, though.
sidequests/sq_gemba_walk_2d/opts/2/r  ·  300a83ac47dc.opus  ·  277 Zeichen
You sketch out 'the Miller Method': four quadrants, a cycle diagram, the word 'mindfulness' at strategic points. HR is electrified. There are now slides with your name on them asserting things you made up out of thin air. This is how management methods come about. All of them.
sidequests/sq_starthilfe/text  ·  2550120d982f.opus  ·  301 Zeichen
Out in the car park Markus waves you over, uncharacteristically subdued. His sports car answers the key with nothing but a tired click. 'Battery. COMPLETELY dead. And I have to be at a client in twenty minutes, Miller. TWENTY.' He looks at the car the way you look at a colleague who has betrayed you.
sidequests/sq_starthilfe/opts/0/r  ·  bc6c46950a35.opus  ·  220 Zeichen
Wrong sentence, wrong man, wrong moment. 'RESCHEDULE?' Markus's voice climbs an octave. 'You do not reschedule a CLOSING!' He runs off to dig up somebody else. You have just insulted a founding principle of his religion.
sidequests/sq_starthilfe/opts/1/r  ·  e83b2636e507.opus  ·  284 Zeichen
Egon appears with a jump starter that looks as though it had been stripped out of a submarine. Two movements, one spark, the engine roars. Markus tears out of the yard. Egon watches him go: 'Weren't the battery. The lad drives too many short journeys.' Egon simply knows these things.
sidequests/sq_starthilfe/opts/2/r  ·  d133fa75bf88.opus  ·  218 Zeichen
Markus in a taxi is a sight for the history books: a man whose self-image is built on 280 horsepower, in the back of a diesel estate. He makes the appointment. The photograph you did not take would have been priceless.
sidequests/sq_starthilfe_2a/text  ·  cd4c0e42fd56.opus  ·  267 Zeichen
Markus is back, the deal is closed, and now he wants to 'do something nice for our caretaker colleague'. He holds up a bottle of brandy, expensive, with a ribbon. 'But you know him, Miller. You do the handing over. Man to man. I am not good at... that sort of thing.'
sidequests/sq_starthilfe_2a/opts/0/r  ·  fc8a6d5f67ba.opus  ·  237 Zeichen
Egon takes the bottle, examines the label with the expression of a customs officer and then nods slowly. 'Drinkable.' It is the highest honour his house has to bestow. Two worlds of men touched for a moment, and you were the interpreter.
sidequests/sq_starthilfe_2a/opts/1/r  ·  72ef5cef8d99.opus  ·  294 Zeichen
'Man to man means yourself, Markus.' He breathes out as though before a client meeting and marches down to the basement. The handover takes four minutes and looks from a distance like a state visit. Afterwards Markus is oddly quiet. 'That man', he says at last, 'has hands like vices. Respect.'
sidequests/sq_starthilfe_2a/opts/2/r  ·  539afaee05bd.opus  ·  242 Zeichen
Not your gift, not your ritual. The next day the bottle is standing awkwardly outside the basement door with a Post-it ('Thanks! M.'). Egon takes it in without comment. Whether it was booked as a gift or as lost property you will never learn.
sidequests/sq_starthilfe_2b/text  ·  5cbca6d59924.opus  ·  331 Zeichen
Markus comes back thoughtful. Not triumphant, not furious: thoughtful. 'The taxi driver, Miller. Twelve hours a day the man drives. SEVEN days a week. And he was... content?' He sits down. 'We complain from a fairly comfortable position here, do we not?' A thoughtful Markus is the most unsettling thing this building has to offer.
sidequests/sq_starthilfe_2b/opts/0/r  ·  9bcc248fb673.opus  ·  239 Zeichen
Chantal is electrified: 'That is a PURE humility journey!' Two days later a notice goes up: 'Change of Perspective Workshop: A Day in a Taxi (sign up with Marketing)'. The taxi driver, approached as a speaker, has declined. He has to work.
sidequests/sq_starthilfe_2b/opts/1/r  ·  669742fe67d9.opus  ·  273 Zeichen
The two of you talk for a quarter of an hour about work, meaning and the question of why nobody is simply content any more. Markus listens more than he talks - a first. He stands up at the end of it: 'Good meeting.' He means it. It was the first honest meeting of the year.
sidequests/sq_starthilfe_2b/opts/2/r  ·  a70b2af37e40.opus  ·  270 Zeichen
'Anyone who is content does not close, Markus.' He looks briefly baffled - then the relief breaks through: 'TRUE!' He laughs, claps you on the shoulder and is entirely his old self again. You have ended an existential crisis with a bad pun. Somewhere a coach is weeping.
sidequests/sq_starthilfe_2c/text  ·  240a839eb1e3.opus  ·  282 Zeichen
Markus has found a driver: Kevin. With the company van. Kevin has had his licence for three weeks. They come back together - the van has a new, long scratch, the pair of them have visibly taken a vow of silence, and the deal fell through anyway. All in all it was not a good outing.
sidequests/sq_starthilfe_2c/opts/0/r  ·  cac9760cb0a7.opus  ·  235 Zeichen
You report the damage to fleet management, factually and with a date. It is the right thing to do, and both of them know it. Even so, Kevin and Markus treat you for a week like a change in the weather. Correctness rarely gets applause.
sidequests/sq_starthilfe_2c/opts/1/r  ·  f005a74f484f.opus  ·  230 Zeichen
Officially you saw nothing. The scratch was 'always there', as all scratches in this world are. The vow of silence now has three members, and vows of silence with three members statistically last eleven days. The clock is running.
sidequests/sq_starthilfe_2c/opts/2/r  ·  14fda6918078.opus  ·  267 Zeichen
Egon inspects the scratch, fetches polish from an unlabelled tin without a word and makes it disappear in twenty minutes. He asks no questions. He merely adds two names quietly to his inner ledger of debts. Kevin and Markus have no idea what they now owe him. You do.
sidequests/sq_lichterkette/text  ·  bac3f8b83673.opus  ·  377 Zeichen

The fairy lights draw their power from a socket in the opened network cabinet. The floor switch next to it is off. Half the floor is offline. Chantal beams: 'Lovely, isn't it?'
sidequests/sq_lichterkette/opts/0/r  ·  9009abd5bbcf.opus  ·  227 Zeichen
You restore the infrastructure. Chantal holds the powerless fairy lights like an injured animal: 'You have killed the energy of this place.' The floor is back online and already complaining about other things. Office ecosystem.
sidequests/sq_lichterkette/opts/1/r  ·  90b0881a2f33.opus  ·  244 Zeichen
Both are running now: switch and atmosphere. The adapter in the network cabinet breaches roughly four policies, and Chantal very nearly hugs you, and the floor notices none of it. Temporary fixes last longest in this building, as is well known.
sidequests/sq_lichterkette/opts/2/r  ·  563682a62256.opus  ·  261 Zeichen
You run the fairy lights neatly to the nearest office socket, lash everything down with cable ties and lock the network cabinet. The corner glows, the switch runs - and for the first time this corridor has decoration that would survive an electrical inspection.
sidequests/sq_lichterkette_2a/text  ·  53752d3d781c.opus  ·  270 Zeichen
Chantal has dedicated a story to the departed corner: a photo of the dark fairy lights with the caption 'Some people are afraid of energy. #officevibes #rip'. You are not tagged. Everybody knows all the same. Colleagues look at you in the corridor like a candle-snuffer.
sidequests/sq_lichterkette_2a/opts/0/r  ·  46e32a211271.opus  ·  237 Zeichen
You survive the day as 'the one who deleted the vibes'. Next morning the story has gone and the outrage has moved on, to the canteen, which has dropped the rice pudding. The office grapevine has the half-life of a fruit fly. Fortunately.
sidequests/sq_lichterkette_2a/opts/1/r  ·  1ee96058957b.opus  ·  262 Zeichen
You hand over an LED string with a battery box: 'Same vibes, zero infrastructure.' Chantal is moved ('So you DO understand!') and rebuilds the corner, this time off the mains. The story gets a happy-ending update. You are tagged. As 'energy saviour'. It is fine.
sidequests/sq_lichterkette_2a/opts/2/r  ·  20206eddb64d.opus  ·  278 Zeichen
You answer in the company chat with a photo of the floor switch and the caption 'He too may simply BE.' The engineering faction cheers, the feel-good faction does not. You have turned a question of decoration into factions. The corridor now has two opinions and no fairy lights.
sidequests/sq_lichterkette_2b/text  ·  1e050a05084a.opus  ·  270 Zeichen
The multi-way adapter in the network cabinet has acquired company: two phone chargers, a USB fan and a lava lamp of unknown origin. The cabinet stands open and somebody is charging an e-bike battery in front of it. Your infrastructure has become a public extension lead.
sidequests/sq_lichterkette_2b/opts/0/r  ·  dc7623014aac.opus  ·  270 Zeichen
You obtain an extension lead on its own circuit, mount it OPPOSITE the network cabinet and label it: 'Charging Point, Second Floor'. The devices move over voluntarily. People follow infrastructure the way water follows a slope. You only have to build the slope properly.
sidequests/sq_lichterkette_2b/opts/1/r  ·  1b231ffdd7b4.opus  ·  260 Zeichen
By virtue of your office you impound the lava lamp as a 'non-certified heating appliance'. It now stands in the server room. On your desk. It bubbles soothingly. The rest of the temporary fix stays, and it was worth it to you. Some official acts are self-care.
sidequests/sq_lichterkette_2b/opts/2/r  ·  daa2a7a230e9.opus  ·  267 Zeichen
You clear the cabinet out and lock it. The dispossessed grumble, Chantal speaks of 'a step backwards', and the lava lamp stands orphaned in the corridor like a memorial. The switch is on the mains alone again, though, exactly as the electrical plans of 2009 intended.
sidequests/sq_lichterkette_2c/text  ·  047a519386e2.opus  ·  251 Zeichen
On his way through the building Dr Wichtig has stopped in front of the properly installed mindfulness corner. He inspects the neatly run fairy lights, the locked cabinet, the sign. 'Proactive space design with SYSTEM at last. Who is responsible here?'
sidequests/sq_lichterkette_2c/opts/0/r  ·  fb6a603dc137.opus  ·  267 Zeichen
Nobody speaks up. Dr Wichtig records the corner as an 'initiative of unclear origin' - and has its own cost centre set up, 'so the project can scale'. There is now a phantom project with a budget and no people in it. It will be the most efficient project of the year.
sidequests/sq_lichterkette_2c/opts/1/r  ·  38bf51334de5.opus  ·  286 Zeichen
'Concept: Marketing. Ms Chantal.' She is appointed 'Feel-Good Officer', small budget included. Her first act in office: a second corner on the ground floor - for which she this time officially asks IT for 'power consultancy'. You have created a process. Out of a string of fairy lights.
sidequests/sq_lichterkette_2c/opts/2/r  ·  abb86eccd6ec.opus  ·  244 Zeichen
'Installation: IT.' Dr Wichtig nods his approval: 'An admin with an eye for atmosphere. Rare.' Your name has joined his mental list of 'people who finish things'. That list is a curse and a knighthood at once, and nobody ever gets off it again.
sidequests/sq_kopierer_karton/text  ·  8c93610582ce.opus  ·  373 Zeichen

The box now has a nickname and serves as a standing table.
sidequests/sq_kopierer_karton/opts/0/r  ·  c7db094106be.opus  ·  201 Zeichen

sidequests/sq_kopierer_karton/opts/1/r  ·  ec28e6ad00e0.opus  ·  300 Zeichen
You cut the box open and assemble the copier step by step from the manual inside, which you then pocket - a manual like that is gold dust in this building. The device runs. sidequests/sq_kopierer_karton/opts/2/r  ·  529627531af1.opus  ·  224 Zeichen

sidequests/sq_kopierer_karton_2a/text  ·  b723e703a6f8.opus  ·  361 Zeichen
The old copier finally died a week later - and because the new one has secretly been running for ages, hardly anybody noticed. Fourteen people are planning the purchase of a copier while copying their applications on the new one.
sidequests/sq_kopierer_karton_2a/opts/0/r  ·  d9dff282efeb.opus  ·  240 Zeichen
You write the last mail of the thread: status, thanks, 'this distribution list is now closed'. It is a small death and a great deliverance. Officially ending an email distribution list feels like slaying a dragon. It happens about as often.
sidequests/sq_kopierer_karton_2a/opts/1/r  ·  281f1cbc1916.opus  ·  272 Zeichen
Your mail ('The device has been running since last week, assembly complete') ends a six-week thread with one paragraph. Fourteen people learn simultaneously that their subject never was one. Three say thank you. One asks who authorised the assembly. It is always that one.
sidequests/sq_kopierer_karton_2a/opts/2/r  ·  7e09b9ead26f.opus  ·  245 Zeichen

sidequests/sq_kopierer_karton_2b/opts/0/r  ·  21865851c308.opus  ·  271 Zeichen

sidequests/sq_kopierer_karton_2b/opts/1/r  ·  3d6001ab7e33.opus  ·  270 Zeichen

sidequests/sq_kopierer_karton_2b/opts/2/r  ·  ae41f6f24923.opus  ·  299 Zeichen

sidequests/sq_kopierer_karton_2c/text  ·  b1bf1be5c908.opus  ·  301 Zeichen

sidequests/sq_kopierer_karton_2c/opts/0/r  ·  218f6d6db317.opus  ·  285 Zeichen
You throw the warranty deadline into the responsibility distribution list like a piece of meat and lean back. The escalation is a natural spectacle: 14 people, one deadline, no responsibility. Popcorn would be appropriate. Egon will probably end up assembling it. Wordlessly. At night.
sidequests/sq_kopierer_karton_2c/opts/1/r  ·  83da87a8b1b4.opus  ·  262 Zeichen

sidequests/sq_kopierer_karton_2c/opts/2/r  ·  a97f1bf2027e.opus  ·  252 Zeichen

sidequests/sq_alpha_2a/text  ·  5aaef0ba47d5.opus  ·  229 Zeichen

sidequests/sq_alpha_2a/opts/0/r  ·  8cafe3d8980e.opus  ·  229 Zeichen
Three weeks too late, and the silence is heavenly. Markus will never learn that his signals are transmitting into the void - in the Circle a missing reply counts as 'grind mode'. That makes you an official grinder. In your sleep.
sidequests/sq_alpha_2a/opts/1/r  ·  df860d6667d0.opus  ·  225 Zeichen
You send a photo of the overnight server monitoring with the slogan 'While you train, your IT patches'. The Circle explodes with reverence. Markus appoints you 'Tech Alpha'. You have not left the game. You have taken it over.

sidequests/sq_intel_2a/opts/1/r  ·  03903c31aa83.opus  ·  314 Zeichen

sidequests/sq_intel_2a/opts/2/r  ·  17409872cd50.opus  ·  272 Zeichen

You are going through the security door into the office wing when somebody comes hurrying up behind you with his hands full: suit, briefcase, friendly nod, no visible pass. Decency says: hold it. The security training says: never. Both say it very loudly.
sidequests/sq_falle_tuer/opts/0/r  ·  5811749c8810.opus  ·  277 Zeichen
The door clicks shut, the gentleman stands in front of it and rings the bell. It is the new finance director, second day at work, pass still with HR. He is correctly let in, correctly greeted and correctly memorises a face. Yours. You did everything right. It helps not at all.
sidequests/sq_falle_tuer/opts/1/r  ·  2063a5950a44.opus  ·  272 Zeichen
The textbook route, performed live: 'Could I just see your pass?' The moment freezes. What follows is awkward rummaging, a justification, your apology for asking, his apology for rummaging - two minutes of social close combat. Security has won. It was pleasant for nobody.
sidequests/sq_falle_tuer/opts/2/r  ·  82b3aefee7de.opus  ·  299 Zeichen
The gentleman thanks you charmingly. Twenty minutes later he introduces himself to the department: external security auditor, and his first finding is already settled - 'access without pass check, granted by a member of IT, of all people'. The words 'of all people' will be italicised in the report.
sidequests/sq_falle_kuchen/text  ·  0aa0959a7b52.opus  ·  243 Zeichen

sidequests/sq_falle_kuchen/opts/1/r  ·  f1223f0bf3f6.opus  ·  313 Zeichen

sidequests/sq_falle_kuchen/opts/2/r  ·  adc66d7d9d75.opus  ·  262 Zeichen

sidequests/sq_falle_meeting/text  ·  5923a6419fad.opus  ·  262 Zeichen

sidequests/sq_falle_meeting/opts/1/r  ·  95402bdbd6cc.opus  ·  307 Zeichen

sidequests/sq_falle_meeting/opts/2/r  ·  90d911941648.opus  ·  296 Zeichen

sidequests/sq_falle_pflanze/text  ·  fc28877aa567.opus  ·  231 Zeichen

sidequests/sq_falle_pflanze/opts/1/r  ·  b094cdffdabd.opus  ·  324 Zeichen

sidequests/sq_falle_pflanze/opts/2/r  ·  146fb0ebc6c5.opus  ·  345 Zeichen

sidequests/sq_handwerker_wagen/opts/0/r  ·  b6910420bdf8.opus  ·  160 Zeichen

sidequests/sq_handwerker_wagen/opts/1/r  ·  14c61f6256fc.opus  ·  215 Zeichen

sidequests/sq_handwerker_wagen_2a/opts/0/r  ·  497a09948eb4.opus  ·  207 Zeichen

lore/chapters/0  ·  58aa57b86bad.opus  ·  442 Zeichen
Baron Wilhelm von Gier originally founded GlobalCorp in the Sauerland as the "Imperial Manufactory for Forms & Self-Perpetuation". His vision was revolutionary: he wanted to sell problems to which only he had the solution. His first patent was the "Endless Stamping Automaton", a steam-powered machine that approved, rejected and shredded applications all at once. It produced maximum turnover with minimum outcome. A business model was born.
lore/chapters/1  ·  2c6b0c3b1a90.opus  ·  468 Zeichen
During the economic miracle GlobalCorp realised that happy employees are unproductive (because they talk too much). The solution was the invention of the grey shade "RAL 7035". Management introduced the revolutionary concept of the "open space warzone": open-plan offices with no sound insulation, in which the neighbour's typing breaks your will. Coffee was also declared an official staple food – not to stay awake, but to sell the shaking hands as "dynamic energy".
lore/chapters/2  ·  e83edc1f170c.opus  ·  398 Zeichen
GlobalCorp connected the world. At least every part of the world that owned a beeping modem. Management extended the "tie requirement" to telephone calls, in the belief that one could "hear competence down the line". This period also produced the legendary "Human Resources" department. The name said it all: people were finally treated like resources – extractable, consumable and easily replaced.
lore/chapters/3  ·  918bcaab3843.opus  ·  385 Zeichen
Dr. Wichtig Sr. bought "the internet" for 500 million marks. He received an AOL CD-ROM and a 56k modem. To save face, the "cloud" was invented. The fact is: our cloud is not a network. It is a disused salt mine in Bottrop, in which "the Archivist" (an employee who has not seen daylight since 1974) photographs important emails onto microfilm. That explains the loading times at login.
lore/chapters/4  ·  e9b7e397f277.opus  ·  385 Zeichen
Today we are "agile". That means: we run in circles, shout "Sprint!" and hope nobody notices that we have no destination. Our new AI "Halgerd" now monitors every mouse click. It calculates in real time whether your toilet break was "business relevant". Should your productivity drop below 120%, your office chair is automatically adjusted to be less comfortable. Welcome to the future.
